issue.title: bazel re-executing actions after restart if the environment was changed before the restart

repository.name: bazel
repository.description: a fast, scalable, multi-language and extensible build system

issue.body:
### Description of the problem
Changing the environment (such as the PATH) causes bazel to re-execute some actions which seems to be by [design](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/a81264e1043dd90e984d9fcef5ce9962dce90d1d/src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/actions/ActionCacheChecker.java#L286) .
Subsequent builds after the env change don't cause a re-execution, **however** if bazel restarts it triggers unnecessary re-executions (supposedly due to "action command has changed").

A bazel restart without a previous env change **does not** trigger these re-executions.

### If possible, provide a minimal example to reproduce the problem:
$bazel build --explain=/tmp/explain.txt --verbose_explanations src:bazel 
$export PATH=$PATH:/bin
// Following rebuilds as expected
$bazel build --explain=/tmp/explain.txt --verbose_explanations src:bazel 
$bazel shutdown
// The next action triggers unnecessary re-executions.
$bazel build --explain=/tmp/explain.txt --verbose_explanations src:bazel 

### Environment info
* Operating System: Goobuntu


* Bazel version (output of `bazel info release`): 0.5.1

body:
There's a pretty easy workaround.

Modify //tools/bazel in your repo to set the environment when it executes Bazel.  We do something like:

```
ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLES=()
ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLES+=(HOSTNAME="${HOSTNAME}")
ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLES+=(SHELL="${SHELL}")
ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLES+=(USER="${USER}")
ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLES+=(PATH="${PATH}")
ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLES+=(LANG="${LANG}")
ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLES+=(HOME="${HOME}")
ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLES+=(LOGNAME="${LOGNAME}")
ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLES+=(TERM="${TERM}")

if [[ ! -z "${DISPLAY+x}" ]]; then
  ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLES+=(DISPLAY="${DISPLAY}")
fi

exec -a "${VERSION_BAZEL}" env -i \
    "${ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLES[@]}" \
    "${VERSION_BAZEL}-real" "$@"
```

That lets us control which version of bazel is in use for each revision of the repository, and the environment.  That makes it easy to handle compatibility.
Ugh, this could be a problem...
@ulfjack Why would this be a problem?
We have some users who are very eager to use remote caching, and we've been trying to get all the necessary changes into 0.5.2, so this bug could be a problem for them.
I confirm that I see cache misses on changes to PATH in combination with bazel server restarts. :-(
I've started on adding a flag for migration. We can't just remove the env variables, since that is a breaking change.

issue.title: Bazel passes through TMPDIR by default, but sandbox doesn't

labels.name: P2
labels.description: We'll consider working on this in future. (Assignee optional)

repository.name: bazel
repository.description: a fast, scalable, multi-language and extensible build system

issue.body:
We are forwarding TMPDIR to the actions, but aren't making it writable in the sandbox. We shouldn't be inconsistent like that.

We're actually likely going to stop forwarding TMPDIR to the actions due to hermeticity / caching concerns (see https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/2574). Although I suppose we might honor it for locally executed actions, but it must not be part of the cache key.
